podcast.body: Considered one of Radiohead's finest songs and their second most covered track after "Creep," "Fake Plastic Trees" was stylistically inspired by a Jeff Buckley concert in Oxford that Thom Yorke attended while grappling with a creative block for the song. Its recording was a "nightmare," requiring numerous takes—possibly the most for any song on *The Bends*—due to Thom Yorke's severe depression, which caused him to weep frequently. Ultimately, Yorke recorded his part alone with a guitar, with other members and effects added later, as his emotional state made full band recording too challenging. "Es inspirar en Jeff Paky un concierto de Jeff Paky en Noffford, después de que la banda, sobre todo, Antonio Orcubi se entró en una especie de comatascamiento creativo para poder desarrollar bien la idea que tenía de la canción y grabar la fona pesadilla."

podcast.body: Recorded during the challenging sessions for "The Bends" album. After a particularly bad day of yelling, producer Steve Lucky sent the band home, asking only Tom York to stay for a "guide vocal" for this track. Tom sang the song once, then burst into tears from the emotional strain, but his one-take performance was deemed "brilliant" and became the final album version. Legend suggests Tom's vocal was inspired by Jeff Buckley, whom the band had seen perform at a local bar the night before. "Tom sat down and sang the song once. And then he burst into tears because the strain had finally got to him."

podcast.body: When "Fake Plastic Trees" was submitted as a single in the United States, the US distributor deemed it insufficiently commercial, "grunge-like," or similar to "Creep" for the guitar-centric American market. Consequently, the distributor independently commissioned Bob Clearmountain to create an unofficial, "guitar-heavy" alternative remix. This version was distributed to US radio stations and media for airplay and was broadcast on several US radios and published in the press, all without the band's knowledge. Upon discovering this, particularly Thom Yorke, the band was horrified by the "guitar version" and immediately halted its distribution, never wishing to re-edit or re-release it. While many purported pirate versions exist, none have been definitively certified as the original Bob Clearmountain remix, though some cassette recordings from radio broadcasts are rumored to be held by individuals. "Entonces, la distribuidor de RID o jelen los Estados Unidos decidió hacer, por su cuenta, una remetcla o una versión alternativa remetclada en los Estados Unidos."
